title: SAS - A Framework for Symmetry-based Approximate Synthesis
problem: Approximating Boolean multi-output functions to reduce area, latency, and power consumption in digital logic circuits while maintaining acceptable computational accuracy. The challenge is to introduce controlled approximations that maximize gains in non-functional properties.
motivation: Approximate computing provides substantial power and area savings, which are critical for resource-constrained Internet of Things devices with limited energy budgets.
method: SAS approximates Boolean multi-output functions by replacing their output functions with symmetric functions that minimize Hamming distance. The framework employs a parameterized error metric to restrict and control the introduced approximation error across different real-world use cases.
key_novelty: Using symmetric functions with minimal Hamming distance as a mechanism for controlled approximate logic synthesis.
contributions: SAS framework for symmetry-based approximate logic synthesis of Boolean functions
Method to replace output functions with symmetric functions minimizing Hamming distance
Parameterized error metric for restricting approximation error in various applications
Enables significant area, speed, and power improvements for IoT devices

metrics.accuracy: controlled via parameterized Hamming distance metric
